question: My Canadian bank withheld income tax from an ordinary RRSP withdrawal. Is that withholding necessarily the final tax I will owe on the withdrawal?
generated_answer:
You may have other tax obligations when you file your income tax and benefit return. Example

You withdrew $10,000 from your RRSP. Your bank withheld $3,000 in income tax, leaving you with $7,000. You must report the full amount of the withdrawal, $10,000, as income on your return. If you have other sources of income and your total income is above the basic personal amount, you may have to pay more income tax when you file your return. 12. How do I know how much income tax was withheld from my RRSP withdrawal? You will find the amount of income tax withheld on your income tax and benefit return slips. Your financial institution will send you one slip for the income tax withheld and another slip for the withdrawal amount. Example

You withdrew $10,000 from your RRSP. Your bank withheld $3,000 in income tax, leaving you with $7,000. You must report the full amount of the withdrawal, $10,000, as income on your return. You will also receive a T4RSP slip from your financial institution showing the full amount of the withdrawal, $10,000. You will also receive a T4A(P) slip showing the amount of income tax withheld, $3,000. If you had other income from employment, you will also receive a T4 slip from your employer showing the income you earned from them and the income tax they withheld from you. 13. If I withdraw money from my RRSP, do I receive a T4 slip? Yes. If you withdraw money from your RRSP, your financial institution will send you a T4RSP slip. You can also log into My Account to view your tax slips, including your T4RSP. 14. Do I have to report the withdrawal from my RRSP on my tax return? Yes. You have to report the withdrawal from your RRSP as income on line 13000 of your return. You will receive a T4RSP slip from your financial institution showing the amount of the withdrawal. 15. Do I have to file a tax return if I withdraw money from my RRSP? If you are filing a tax return for the first time after you turn 19, you may not need to file a return for the year in which you withdrew money from your RRSP. For more information, go to Do I have to file a return? 16. How do I report the withdrawal from my RRSP on my tax return? Report the withdrawal from your RRSP on line 13000 of your return. Your financial institution will send you a T4RSP slip showing the amount of the withdrawal. 17. Can I claim a deduction on my tax return for the amount I contributed to my RRSP? You can claim a deduction on your tax return for the amount you contributed to your RRSP. The maximum deduction you can claim is 18% of your net earned income from employment, up to the annual limit. For more information, go to Line 20800 – RRSP deduction. 18. What if I contributed to my RRSP but I did not claim the deduction on my tax return? You may be able to claim the deduction on your tax return in a future year. The maximum deduction you can claim is 18% of your net earned income from employment, up to the annual limit. For more information, go to Line 20800 – RRSP deduction. 19. Can I contribute to my RRSP and claim the deduction on my tax return in the same year? Yes. You can contribute to your RRSP and claim the deduction on your tax return in the same year. The maximum deduction you can claim is 18% of your net earned income from employment, up to the annual limit. For more information, go to Line 20800 – RRSP deduction. 20. Can I contribute to more than one RRSP in a year? Yes. You can contribute to more than one RRSP in a year. The maximum deduction you can claim is 18% of your net earned income from employment, up to the annual limit. For more information, go to Line 20800 – RRSP deduction. 21. Can I contribute to my RRSP and someone else's RRSP in the same year? Yes. You can contribute to your RRSP and someone else's RRSP in the same year.
